target_customer: Procurement departments at large enterprises (Fortune 500 and Global 2000)
problem: Purchase requests need vendor research, negotiation, approvals and delivery tracking, which consumes procurement teams' hours; early askLio turned free-text requests into structured ones that fit contracts and catalogs.
business_model: Enterprise B2B software and services, with consulting-style transformation work (pricing not found)

founders.name: Vlad Keil
founders.background_notes: Consulted enterprises on procurement per the YC page.

founders.name: Lukas Heinzmann
founders.background_notes: Technical lead for the myAudi app per the YC page.

founders.name: Till Wagner
education: Bachelor's and Master's degrees (institutions not stated)
founders.background_notes: Worked on product building at AI startups including one in San Francisco per the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Multi-agent systems that integrate with ERP, P2P, contracts and email at large enterprises require deep integrations and reliable LLM orchestration; the 2023 version was a simpler Teams copilot.

defensibility.rationale: Enterprise integrations and procurement domain workflows create stickiness, but incumbents such as SAP Ariba and Coupa can add agents.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents added AI features, but Lio kept growing and raised a Series A in 2026; sources name Zip and SAP Ariba as competitors without dates.

market_need_then: Procurement requests were often unstructured and routed manually; large language models in 2023 made reading free-text requests and matching them to contracts feasible.

branding.domain_note: Moved to lio.ai; earlier name used asklio branding (asklio.ai per a directory listing).

identity.voice_and_tone: Enterprise claims about an AI procurement workforce; hosts a Bots & Buyers summit

rebrands.why: Not stated in any source found; no official announcement located.

branding.community_and_virality: Company runs a Bots & Buyers summit and gets trade press from Procurement Magazine; no wider community evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Trade press and event but no consumer or developer brand; the shorter name fits enterprise positioning, though 'LIO' trademarks exist for unrelated owners.

pivots.from: askLio, an AI copilot for turning purchase requests into structured requests inside MS Teams
pivots.to: Lio, a multi-agent AI procurement department
pivots.why: Not stated by the company; shown by the YC page and the rename.

outcome_analysis: Lio grew from a YC S23 copilot into a team of about 80 and raised a $30M Series A led by a16z in March 2026, with the company claiming 150 to 175 enterprise customers. The shift from a request-intake copilot to full multi-agent procurement matched the 2024 to 2026 agent wave. Round and traction figures are press-release claims, and the early seed amount is only aggregator-reported.
notes: Series A confirmed by the PR Newswire release and a second outlet (ITDigest), also cited on the YC page via TechCrunch dated 2026-03-05. Total raised reported as $33M, implying about $3M earlier; earlier rounds not itemized. One profile says $500K from YC and Pioneer Fund in 2023 (aggregator only, not recorded as a round). Headquarters conflicts across sources (Munich, New York, San Francisco). No competitor source dated near the 2023 batch was found, so the list is empty; Zip, SAP Ariba, Omnea, Arkestro are named by undated profiles. Company page claims 175+ customers while press says 150+, both self-reported.
